title: International logistics platform
description: A Django backend replacing fragmented spreadsheets with shipment, branch, and multi-currency financial workflows.
proof: Supported operations across 6 countries and 5 languages.
context: A logistics client relied on fragmented Excel and Word workflows for shipments, branch operations, and financial records. The platform centralized these processes for approximately 30 employees, with restricted customer and transport-personnel access.
contribution: Led technical delivery for a seven-developer freelance team. Owned requirements discussions, backend architecture and implementation, code review, deployment configuration, and maintenance, working with two backend teammates and the frontend lead.

architecture.summary: The React frontend, Django backend, PostgreSQL database, and supporting services ran on one Alibaba Cloud ECS instance. Delivery included Linux, Docker, Nginx, HTTPS, and backups.

components.name: Operations interface
components.detail: Shipment, branch, customer, and financial workflows.

components.name: Django backend
components.detail: Role-based access and guarded business operations.

components.name: PostgreSQL & ECS
components.detail: Persistent records and a single-instance deployment.

decisions.title: Confirm transport updates at the branch
decisions.description: Transport personnel could submit status updates, but the originating branch had to confirm them. This made the operational approval rule part of backend behavior.

decisions.title: Preserve currency context
decisions.description: Financial records retained the original amount, received currency, and exchange rate against Chinese yuan. Those details preserve the context needed to interpret multi-currency transactions.

decisions.title: Keep delivery and recovery explicit
decisions.description: The deployment used a single ECS instance, with daily and on-demand backups. Image building and staging preparation were automated; production replacement remained manual, with the associated operational responsibility.

results: Implemented four role-based access models for administrators, branch staff, customers, and transport personnel.
Configured deployment and backups, and handled subsequent maintenance and improvements.
limitations: The client and source code are confidential. Technical lead describes responsibility within a small freelance team. This was a single-instance deployment, not a claim of high availability or large-scale traffic.
resourceNote: Public source and a live demo are unavailable for this confidential client system. I can discuss the architecture and my contribution without disclosing client data.
